attribution_limitations: The case text calls the right lung nodular opacities radiologically suggestive of metastatic lesions on non-contrast CT, while the discussion states that lung metastases were identified in this patient; no biopsy or pathologic confirmation of lung disease is reported. The discussion wording is a restatement of the imaging finding rather than a contradiction, so it is recorded as an ambiguity, not a source conflict.
The discussion says serum tumor markers in NGOC are generally within normal ranges, consistent with this case, but the case section reports no tumor marker result and names no marker.

Hyperthyroidism is stated as observed in this case only in the discussion; the case section reports only a slightly elevated total thyroxine and no thyroid-stimulating hormone or free thyroxine values, so the diagnostic basis is not stated.

Serum hCG is reported as more than 297,475 IU/L at the referral stage, 282,995 IU/L in the laboratory tests reported after the examination, and more than 297,000 IU/L in the abstract. The abstract value is most likely the referral-stage result rounded down (a rounding-level difference, not a conflict), but the source never says so; the 282,995 IU/L value is a different result whose order relative to the referral-stage value is not stated.

The abstract and the case text give slightly different descriptions of the preoperative imaging (the abstract mentions necrosis and cystic changes on ultrasonography and CT; the case text reports cystic or necrotic areas on ultrasound and a central necrotic area on CT). The abstract statements are kept as separate observations.

Lower abdominal pain is reported for over three weeks, yet the onset of vaginal bleeding two weeks before admission is described without accompanying pain; the earlier pain was described as intermittent.
